body.name: Complete \((2,2,3)\) source-table trace
body.construction: Take the ordered cycle \(1\to2\to3\to1\), \(\mathcal X_1=\mathcal X_2=\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal X_3=\{0,1,2\}\), and sources \(s_{12},s_{23},e_2\) with incidences \(\{1,2\},\{2,3\},\{2\}\).  Let \(\mathcal I\), \(\mathcal J\), and \(\mathcal K\) be respectively the eight maps \(i:\mathcal X_3\to\mathcal X_1\), four maps \(j:\mathcal X_1\to\mathcal X_2\), and nine maps \(k:\mathcal X_2\to\mathcal X_3\), all ordered lexicographically.  Set \(\Omega_{s_{12}}=\mathcal I\), \(\Omega_{s_{23}}=\mathcal K\), and \(\Omega_{e_2}=\mathcal J^{\mathcal I\times\mathcal K}\).  For \(\eta\in\Omega_{e_2}\), the decoder sends \((i,k,\eta)\) to \((i,\eta(i,k),k)\).  With independent source masses \(a_i,c_k,d_\eta\), the induced response-profile probabilities are \(\pi_{ijk}=a_ic_k\sum_{\eta:\eta(i,k)=j}d_\eta\).  The legality checker retains exactly the 240 triples for which \(k\circ j\circ i\) has one fixed point and rejects 48.  The boundary rows are \(u_a=\sum_i a_i\mathbf1\{i(a)=1\}\) and \(v_b=\sum_k c_k\mathbf1\{k(b)=2\}\).  Supply clamp regimes \(\operatorname{do}(X_3=a)\) for \(a=0,1,2\) and \(\operatorname{do}(X_2=b)\) for \(b=0,1\).  For each \(A_{ab}=\{X_1(X_3=a)=1,X_3(X_2=b)=2\}\), \(a,b\in\{0,1\}\), with \(B\) the sure event, the ordered recursion takes transitions (1), (2), (3), and (6), and \(\mathsf{SATerm}\) returns \(C_{ab}(p)=u_av_b\).  Its exact record is \(\mathsf{VALID\mbox{-}INPUT}\), \(\mathsf{LEGAL}=240/288\), \(\mathsf{SOURCES}=(8,9,4^{72})\), \(\mathsf{SEPARATOR\mbox{-}QE}=\mathsf{UNSAT}\), \(\mathsf{REMAINDER}=0\), \(\mathsf{DIVISOR}=1\), \(\mathsf{INTERFACE}=\mathsf{MATCH}\), and \(\mathsf{OUTPUT}=u_av_b\).  Thus the trace uses one genuine private-source simplex and never replaces the source-factorized law by an unrestricted simplex on the 240 legal rows.
